title: Passports for the English trip and Purnell staying in California
summary: On the way to England the band needs passports, and he recalls Purnell staying on the West Coast and the Cavalier records.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, we'd done that for quite a long time. And I guess you came back then, you made the English trip, did you? Yeah, it was, yeah, we went, it was from there. And we was working at the Sinton Hotel. Mm-hmm. When we got news that we was going overseas. Mm-hmm. So, we came on back home after we finished the engagement with Andrew Sinton. We came back home, that's the time I was trying to find Russell. Yeah. To see if I get our passport. Passport. Because George had his, you see. Yeah. Whether it was Jack, Howard, Jim, Joe Robichaud, and myself that had to get passports. When did Joe Robichaud come in and Purnell leave? Well, that was after Purnell had stayed out in Frisco. Yeah. You see, that was the time that George first went overseas by himself. Yeah. That was back in 56. Yeah, that's about it, yeah. Yeah. Because at that time, we was playing at Tin Angel. Yeah. And out and stayed out on the West Coast. Yeah, he stayed out on the West Coast then with it to finish out, you know. And he said he was going to decide to stay out in Los Angeles. I said, well, Elton, I said, it's up to you. I said, you do the suit yourself. But I said, the rest of the band is going back home. I said, because nothing to us is staying out here. I said, our families is back home. It's better that we going back. Well, at that time we had Bob Thomas on the trombone and Tom Jefferson on trumpet.
That was the band that made those records on Cavalier, remember? Yeah, Cavalier.
Yeah, that's another record I miss getting. I never did get a chance of getting one.
That was without Lawrence though, you know?
